commands.label: NAVIGATE
commands.description: Navigates the browser to a specific URL and waits for the page to finish loading, for at most nav_timeout (30s by default). A navigation the browser could not make — a host that does not resolve, a refused connection — fails the step with the browser's own error, on both backends. A plain http:// URL is loaded as given: Chromium is launched with its HTTPS-First and HTTPS-Upgrades features off, which from Chrome 154 otherwise refuse an http-only site with net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT. When the time runs out, a document that has already been parsed is carried on with and a warning logged: it is a usable page held up by a resource that may never arrive. One that has not been parsed fails the step with a navigation timeout.

commands.label: OPEN APP
commands.description: Attaches to an Electron/Desktop app window instead of navigating to a URL. Use as the first step for executable_path targets.

commands.label: SWITCH TO TAB
commands.description: Makes another open tab the one the next steps run on, and brings it to the front. The argument is a position — 1 is the tab the hunt began on, then each tab a step opened, in the order they were opened, counting open tabs only — or quoted text, which picks the first open tab whose title or URL contains it, ignoring case. SWITCH TAB is the same verb. Only the tab the hunt began on and the tabs it has followed are counted; other tabs the browser has open are not. A position past the last open tab, text no tab has, or an argument that is neither fails the step. Following a newly opened tab needs no SWITCH; going back to one that is still open does.

commands.label: CLICK
commands.description: Clicks a resolved element. Detected by the 'click' verb (case-insensitive). Element type hint (button, link, element) after the target is optional but recommended for scoring accuracy. The click is dispatched at the centre of the element, the pointer moved there first, so it would go to whatever is on top of it there. When that is not the element, something inside it, something it is inside, or the <label> it belongs to, the engine waits up to about 1.5s for it to clear and then fails the step naming what is in the way (for example an open date picker or a modal backdrop) — nothing is clicked. After the click the engine waits for any navigation it set off: it marks the document first, and if the page starts to leave it (beforeunload) waits, for at most nav_timeout, until another document has replaced it and finished loading. Until then the old document still reports readyState 'complete', so the next step would run on a page that is about to go. Interaction mode: clickable.

commands.label: DOUBLE CLICK
commands.description: Double-clicks a resolved element. Detected by the 'double' + 'click' verbs (case-insensitive). A covered target fails the step, as for CLICK. The snapshot cache is dropped afterwards, so the next step sees what the double click opened. Interaction mode: clickable.

commands.label: CHECK
commands.description: Checks a checkbox element. Detected by the 'check' verb (case-insensitive). The target may be the box itself, its

commands.label: UNCHECK
commands.description: Unchecks a checkbox element. Detected by the 'uncheck' verb (case-insensitive). Resolved and verified as CHECK is. Interaction mode: clickable.

commands.label: FILL
commands.description: Types text into a resolved input/textarea element. Detected by the 'fill' verb (case-insensitive). Element type hint (field, input) is optional but recommended. The element typed into must be a field that takes text (an input, textarea, editable element, or a <select>): a caption, heading or table header that matches the target is how the field beside or below it is found, and a step that resolves to no field fails with failure_reason not_found instead of passing with the value written nowhere. A text field the target names that is disabled fails the step with failure_reason action_failed and says so, rather than resolving to some text that mentions it. An <input> or <textarea> is scrolled to the middle of its scrolling boxes first, and if something else is still on top of its centre after about 1.5s the step fails naming it and nothing is typed. Interaction mode: input.

commands.label: TYPE
commands.description: Types text into a resolved element. Detected by the 'type' verb (case-insensitive). The element must be a field that takes text, as for FILL. Interaction mode: input.

commands.label: SELECT
commands.description: Selects an option from a native <select> or custom dropdown. Detected by the 'select' or 'choose' verbs (case-insensitive). Element type hint (dropdown) is optional but recommended. On a native <select> the option is matched against both its label and its value, whitespace-normalised and case-insensitively; the option is set through the native value setter and followed by input and change events, and a change that reloads the page is waited for as after a CLICK. An option that matches nothing fails the step with failure_reason not_found, and the error lists the options the page does have. A custom dropdown follows the same rule: after it is opened, an option no element in the list matches fails the step rather than clicking whatever ranked first. Interaction mode: select.

commands.label: HOVER
commands.description: Hovers over a resolved element. Detected by the 'hover' verb (case-insensitive). Interaction mode: hover.

commands.label: DRAG
commands.description: Drags one element and drops it onto another. Detected by the 'drag' + 'drop' verbs (case-insensitive). A source or destination that nothing on the page matches fails the step with failure_reason not_found. The drag is a pointer drag — press on the source, moves across, release on the target — which is what pointer-event libraries listen to, and on Chromium also starts a native HTML5 drag. Firefox starts none from WebDriver actions, so there a source that is or sits inside an element with draggable="true" is dragged by dispatching the HTML5 drag events in the page instead: dragstart and drag on it, dragenter and dragover on the target, drop only if dragover was cancelled (a target that does not cancel it refuses the drop, as in a browser), then dragend, all sharing one DataTransfer. That substitution is made in the innermost frame under the drag, same-origin or cross-origin, so a draggable inside an iframe is dragged the same way; a drag whose two ends are in different frames is sent to the page as it is. Interaction mode: drag.

commands.label: SCROLL DOWN
commands.description: Scrolls the main page down by one viewport height, or scrolls a container to the bottom when 'inside the <container>' is appended. The container is resolved like any other target and may be a {placeholder}; one that is not on the page fails the step with failure_reason not_found rather than scrolling whatever ranked first.

commands.label: WAIT
commands.description: Hard sleep for N seconds. Only matched when other WAIT variants (WAIT FOR RESPONSE, WAIT FOR element) do not match first. N may be a {placeholder}; anything that is not a number by the time the step runs fails it. The snapshot cache is dropped afterwards: what was read before the wait says nothing about the page after it.

commands.label: WAIT FOR element
commands.description: Explicit wait for a quoted element to reach a desired state. States: visible (the default), hidden / disappear, enabled, disabled. Polls every 250ms for up to 15s, invalidating the snapshot cache each time so the wait can see the change it is waiting for. A state other than these fails the step at once. Presence is judged at ThresholdAmbiguous — the same bar the rest of the engine uses to call a target resolved — because the scorer always ranks something and 'a top candidate exists' is not 'the target is present'. Only an element that carries the target whole can be the one awaited: as a phrase in its text, label, placeholder, aria-label, title, name, value or test id, or as its id. Sharing a word with the target is not enough, or 'A checkbox' would stay present for as long as any sentence on the page mentioned checkboxes.

commands.label: WAIT FOR SELECTOR
commands.description: Explicit wait for a CSS selector to appear in the DOM. Bypasses the scorer entirely — the caller gave an exact selector, so it is honoured literally. Prefer it over WAIT FOR when targeting by tag or class rather than visible text (e.g. 'ytd-video-renderer'). Parsed ahead of the other WAIT FOR forms, which would otherwise swallow it.

commands.label: WAIT FOR RESPONSE
commands.description: Blocks until a network response whose URL ends with the pattern arrives (suffix match, on both the CDP and the BiDi backend), for at most nav_timeout; the step fails when none does. Only responses that arrive after the step has started are seen: one that the previous step triggered and that had already come back by then is not, while one it triggered that is still on its way is. Firefox reports a response only for a request that began while the session was subscribed, so a BiDi page subscribes to network.responseCompleted when it opens rather than when the wait starts.

commands.label: EXTRACT
commands.description: Extracts the text content of a resolved element and stores it into a runtime variable for use in subsequent steps. A target that names a form control reads what the control currently holds instead of the text around it — this is how a value written by FILL is read back. The control is named when its label, placeholder, aria-label, title, name, id or test id is the target (case, surrounding whitespace and a trailing ':' or '*' aside), when the text the target matched turns out to be its

commands.label: VERIFY
commands.description: Asserts that an element or text is present, not present, enabled, disabled, checked, or not checked. Fails the mission on mismatch. State is read off the element whether or not it is disabled — 'is disabled' finds the disabled control, and a read-only checkbox still reports 'is checked'. Text that cannot be seen is not present: what is display:none, visibility:hidden, or transparent — opacity under 0.01, on the element or on any element around it — is left out, so a faded-out notice or a button hidden by opacity:0 makes 'is NOT present' pass. Text shown once and also present transparently elsewhere is still present. Text compares the way it reads: case-insensitively, with every run of whitespace, line breaks and no-break spaces included, counted as one space on both sides, so two spans shown on one line as 'Shopping cart (1)' match although the page's innerText breaks them apart. A text check that could not read the page at all fails rather than concluding the text is absent. The text read includes that of every shadow root however deeply nested, a top-level child of each at a time, so text drawn by web components (archive.org, Lit and Stencil apps) is seen, and so is the text of every <iframe>, nested ones included. A cross-origin iframe's text is read as well. A text check polls for up to the step timeout until it is satisfied: 'is present' until the text appears, 'is NOT present' until it is gone — so a negated check passes on the first look when the text is absent, and waits for text that is still disappearing.

commands.label: VERIFY strict text
commands.description: Strict text verification. Resolves the element via heuristics, reads locator.inner_text().strip(), and asserts exact equality against the expected text.

commands.label: VERIFY strict placeholder
commands.description: Strict placeholder verification. Resolves the element via heuristics, reads its placeholder attribute, and asserts exact equality against the expected placeholder. As with the value form, a <label> is never the element resolved and a disabled field is.

commands.label: VERIFY strict value
commands.description: Strict value verification. Resolves the element via heuristics, reads its current value via locator.input_value() with a value-attribute fallback, normalizes missing values to an empty string, and asserts exact equality against the expected value. A

commands.label: VERIFY SOFTLY
commands.snippet: VERIFY SOFTLY that '${1:target}' is ${2|present,NOT present,ENABLED,DISABLED,checked,NOT checked|}
commands.description: Non-fatal assertion. Same as VERIFY but does not stop execution on failure. Failures are collected as soft errors with 'warning' status. One look at the page, no retry loop: the text form checks the page text, the state form (enabled, disabled, checked, visible, …) reads that state off the resolved element.

commands.label: VERIFY VISUAL
commands.description: Compares how the named element looks against a saved baseline image. The element is resolved like any other target (a name nothing on the page matches fails with not_found), scrolled into view, and cropped out of a viewport screenshot. The baseline is visual_baselines/<element-name>_<hash of the step text>.png beside the .hunt file (the working directory when the hunt has no file); the first run saves it and passes. Later runs fail when the size differs or when more than 1% of pixels differ. Baselines are browser-specific: Chromium and Firefox do not render alike.

commands.label: PRESS ENTER
commands.description: Presses the Enter key on the currently focused element. Useful for submitting forms after filling a field.

commands.label: PRESS
commands.description: Presses any key or key combination globally (e.g. PRESS Escape, PRESS Control+A), or on a specific resolved element when 'on <target>' is appended. A chord holds its modifiers (Control/Ctrl, Alt/Option, Meta/Cmd, Shift) around the last key. With 'on <target>' the target is focused first — a field if one matches, otherwise anything clickable — and a target nothing matches fails the step instead of pressing the key wherever focus happens to be. A key that sets off a navigation, such as Enter in a form field, is waited for as after a CLICK.

commands.label: RIGHT CLICK
commands.description: Right-clicks a resolved element to open a context menu. A covered target fails the step, as for CLICK. The snapshot cache is dropped afterwards, so the next step can target an item of the menu it opened.

commands.label: UPLOAD
commands.description: Uploads a file to a file-input element. Both file path and target must be quoted. Path resolved relative to the .hunt file directory, then CWD, and handed to the browser as an absolute path. A path that names no file fails the step before the browser is asked.

commands.label: MOCK
commands.description: Answers matching network requests from a local file instead of from the network, by request interception: the Fetch domain over CDP, network intercepts over WebDriver BiDi. The pattern is matched against the end of the request URL, query string included, and '*' stands for any run of characters — "/api/users" answers https://host/v1/api/users, "/api/users*" also answers it with a query string. Any request is covered, whatever makes it: a navigation, fetch, XMLHttpRequest, an image. A rule holds for the rest of the session, across navigations; a later MOCK for the same method and pattern replaces it. The response has status 200 and a Content-Type of application/json for a .json file and text/plain otherwise. A cross-origin request gets the CORS headers it needs, and its preflight is answered too. The HTTP cache is bypassed from the first MOCK on, since a cached response is never requested. The mock file is resolved relative to the .hunt file directory, then CWD. Supported HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

commands.label: CALL HOST
commands.description: Invokes a handler registered by the host inline. In Go the handler is registered via the embedding API (RegisterGoCall); through a language binding it is a function in the client process, reached by a reverse call over the session protocol. Supports positional arguments ('with args:' sugar), optional 'into {var}' / 'to {var}' capture, and @script alias rewriting for CALL HOST {alias}.func syntax. CALL GO and CALL PYTHON are accepted spellings of the same command and parse identically.

commands.label: SET
commands.description: Sets a runtime variable mid-flight. Both {braced} and bare key forms accepted. Quoted values are auto-unquoted. Available for {placeholder} substitution in all subsequent steps.

commands.label: PRINT
commands.description: Logs a message to the run output, with {placeholder} variables substituted and a single layer of surrounding quotes stripped. No element resolution. (CmdPrint).

commands.label: SCREENSHOT
commands.description: Captures a full-page PNG on demand into screenshots/<name>.png under the CWD (auto-named when no label is given).

commands.label: HIGHLIGHT
commands.description: Flashes a border around a resolved element for two seconds. Purely diagnostic — it changes nothing on the page. A target that does not resolve is an error rather than a silent no-op, since a highlight nobody can see is not worth passing.

commands.label: FULL SCAN
commands.description: Scans the current page and prints every interactive control as Markdown tables grouped by landmark ancestor, one '## group' heading per landmark with a role/label/tag/editable/locator table. Console only, no file output. Groups are emitted in sorted order so two scans of the same page diff cleanly. Markdown rather than JSON because the audience is a person reading a terminal or a model reading a prompt.

commands.label: SCAN PAGE
commands.description: Scans the current page and prints a draft .hunt to the console, optionally writing it to a file with 'into {filename}' or 'to {filename}' — relative to the working directory, with any missing directories created. Complements the `scan` CLI subcommand, which needs a URL: these verbs work on a page you can only reach by driving there — behind a login, or three steps into a flow.

commands.label: DEBUG
commands.description: Pauses execution at this step. In interactive terminal mode (--debug), prompts the user; in pipe mode (--break-lines), emits the debug pause protocol marker. PAUSE is accepted as an alias.

commands.label: DEBUG VARS
commands.description: Prints the current state of all runtime variables to the console for diagnostic purposes.

commands.label: DONE
commands.description: Explicitly ends the mission. Any steps after DONE are not executed.

commands.label: STEP
commands.description: Declares a hierarchical STEP block. All action lines following this header belong to this block until the next STEP header. The number is optional. Used for HTML report accordions and console grouping.

commands.label: USE
commands.description: Expands an imported STEP block inline at parse time. The block must have been imported via @import:. Aliased names (from 'as' clause) are supported. Case-insensitive matching.

commands.label: IF
commands.description: Block-style conditional branching. Body lines are indented by 4 extra spaces. Supports ELIF and ELSE branches, in the mission body and inside [SETUP] / [TEARDOWN] alike. Nesting supported. Conditions: element exists, text present, variable comparison/contains/truthy; their keywords are case-insensitive ('is NOT present') and read outside the quotes, so a label or a compared value may contain them. The target may be in single or double quotes and may be a {placeholder}. 'not exists' and 'does not exist' are the same negation. An element counts as existing only when it carries the target itself, not merely because it ranked first.

commands.label: ELIF
commands.description: Alternative branch in an IF block. Multiple ELIF branches are allowed. Must follow IF or another ELIF. Cannot appear after ELSE.

commands.label: ELSE
commands.description: Default branch in an IF block. Only one ELSE is allowed and must be the last branch.

commands.label: REPEAT
commands.description: Fixed-count loop. Body lines are indented by 4 extra spaces. The counter variable is {i} unless the header names another with 'REPEAT N TIMES as {name}:', and counts from 0. N may be a {placeholder} set while the hunt runs; a count that is not a number by then fails the step instead of looping zero times. Nesting supported.

commands.label: FOR EACH
commands.description: Iterate over comma-separated values from a variable. On each iteration the loop variable is set to the next value. Nesting supported. A collection that is not the name of a variable is taken as the list itself, which is also what a collection declared with @var: is by the time the loop runs: @var: values are substituted into the line at parse time, unless the hunt assigns to the name or is data-driven (see @var:).

commands.label: WHILE
commands.description: Repeat while condition is true. Uses same conditions as IF blocks. The condition is evaluated against the page as it is at each pass, not against a cached snapshot. Safety limit: 100 iterations. Nesting supported.

metadata.label: @context:
metadata.description: Strategic context for the mission (documentation / agent hint). Placed at the top of the file.

metadata.label: @title:
metadata.description: Short display name for the test suite. @blueprint: is accepted as a backward-compatible alias.

metadata.label: @tags:
metadata.description: Comma-separated run tags for CLI --tags filtering. Files are selected when at least one tag matches.

metadata.label: @var:
metadata.description: Declares a variable pre-populated into runtime memory before any step runs. Available as {key} placeholder in all steps. A value may use variables declared above it; they are resolved once, in file order. The value is written into each line at parse time unless the hunt can change it: a name the hunt assigns to anywhere (SET {key} = …, … into {key}, FOR EACH {key} IN …, REPEAT … as {key}) stays a placeholder that the runtime resolves, starting from the declared value, and in a hunt with @data: every name does, so a column of the data file overrides the declaration of the same name.

metadata.label: @script:
metadata.description: Declares a file-local Go function alias for later CALL GO usage. Supported forms: module alias (`@script: {auth} = scripts.auth_helpers` -> `CALL GO {auth}.issue_token`) and callable alias (`@script: {issue_token} = scripts.auth_helpers.issue_token` -> `CALL GO {issue_token}`). Alias names must match placeholder identifiers (`^[A-Za-z_]\w*$`). Targets must be registered Go function references (package.function).

metadata.label: @data:
metadata.description: Points to a JSON (array-of-objects) or CSV file for data-driven testing. The engine reruns the entire mission for each row, injecting values as {placeholders}.

metadata.label: @schedule:
metadata.snippet: @schedule: ${1|every 30 seconds,every 1 minute,every 5 minutes,every 15 minutes,every 1 hour,daily at 09:00,every monday|}
metadata.description: Declares a schedule for daemon mode (manul daemon). Supported: every N seconds/minutes/hours, every minute/hour, daily at HH:MM, every <weekday>, every <weekday> at HH:MM.

metadata.label: @import:
metadata.description: Imports named STEP blocks from another .hunt file. Supports named imports (@import: Login, Logout from lib.hunt), wildcard (@import: * from lib.hunt) and aliases (@import: Login as AuthLogin from lib.hunt). The source is a path relative to the importing file's directory, or an absolute path. Imported blocks are available for USE directives. @var: declarations from the source file, and from whatever it imports in turn, are inherited at LEVEL_IMPORT (lowest priority): they stay {placeholders} in the imported steps, so the importing hunt's own @var:, a data row or a global overrides them. When two imports declare the same name, the first keeps it. A count the parser reads itself (REPEAT {n} TIMES, WAIT {n}) is the exception, written in from the source file's own value.

metadata.label: @export:
metadata.description: Declares which STEP blocks are importable by other .hunt files. Multiple @export: lines are allowed. @export: * makes all blocks available. When no @export: is declared and a wildcard @import: * is used, all blocks are available (open by default).

hookBlocks.label: [SETUP]
hookBlocks.snippet:
[SETUP]
    PRINT "${1:Preparing setup}"
    CALL GO ${2:module}.${3:function}${4: with args: "${5:arg}"}${6: into {${7:variable}}}
[END SETUP]
hookBlocks.description: Block of PRINT and CALL GO lines executed BEFORE the browser launches. If any line fails, the mission is marked as broken and browser steps are skipped. Teardown still runs when setup fails. Target functions must be synchronous.

hookBlocks.label: [TEARDOWN]
hookBlocks.snippet:
[TEARDOWN]
    PRINT "${1:Cleaning up}"
    CALL GO ${2:module}.${3:function}${4: with args: "${5:arg}"}
[END TEARDOWN]
hookBlocks.description: Cleanup block executed after the mission body in a finally block. It runs whether [SETUP] and the mission passed or failed — a setup that got halfway still has something to clean up. Failure is logged but does not override the mission result.

qualifiers.description: Biases candidate ranking by Euclidean distance to a resolved anchor element. Used for repeated buttons, links, and fields located close to a known label or neighboring control. The anchor is resolved among the page's snapshot elements, which include headings (h1–h6) as well as controls, cells and text blocks, so a product title in an <h3> anchors its own card rather than the list around it.
Prefers candidates inside header or nav ancestry, or within the top 15% of the viewport.
Prefers candidates inside footer ancestry, or within the bottom 15% of the viewport.

Resolves the container first and keeps only its descendants, then finds the row text among them, climbs to its table row (tr), and restricts candidate scoring to that row before normal action scoring continues. 'INSIDE 'Users' row with 'John'' is therefore the John row of the Users table, even when another table has a John row too. Without 'row with', INSIDE restricts to the container's descendants alone. The container is the best-ranked of the top five matches that has snapshot elements inside it, so a heading that names a section never stands in for the section.
